newsitem.title: GERMANY: Opel says to cut about 200 jobs in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Opel says to cut about 200 jobs in 1997.

text.p: German carmaker Adam Opel AG, a unit of U.S. carmaker General Motors Corp, said on Thursday it did not expect major job cuts in 1997 and said there were few prospects for adding jobs next year.
Opel management board member Wolfgang Strinz, who is responsible for personnel issues, said about 200 jobs would likely be cut this year and reduce the workforce to about 44,500 people.

But he declined to give concrete figures over other possible jobs cuts at an Opel news conference. Recent media reports said Opel may consider cutting up to 10,000 jobs in the coming years as GM boosts production in emerging markets.

Talks between Opel and its works council over extending a job security pact for German workers have broken down. Opel management wants a deal through 2000, while the council wants a contract at least through 2005.
